banner: OpenCode 密钥泄露 波及 1.4% 用户
banner_en: OpenCode breach exposes keys for 1.4% of users

image.caption: 本期要图：OpenCode 在 GitHub 上的项目主页配图。（图：GitHub/anomalyco/opencode）
image.caption_en: Today's front-page image: OpenCode's own GitHub repository banner graphic. (Image: GitHub/anomalyco/opencode)

actions.text: 如果你用的是 OpenCode 的云端 Console（不是本地 CLI 自带 key 那种），今晚就去 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 后台撤销旧 key、生成新的，5 分钟。背景：OpenCode Console 后台一套要下线的老系统被未授权访问过，存在里面的第三方 key 可能已经泄露，官方说影响了 1.4% 的用户，但没说清楚具体是谁。
actions.text_en: If you use OpenCode's hosted Console (not the local CLI with your own key), go revoke your old OpenAI and Anthropic keys and generate new ones tonight, 5 minutes. Background: a legacy system behind OpenCode Console that was being decommissioned saw unauthorized access, third-party keys stored there may be exposed, and the company says 1.4% of users were affected without saying exactly who.

actions.text: 挑一个你自己在跑的、有真实 API 权限的 agent（哪怕只是脚本里的一把 key），给它加一个每小时调用次数上限或每月预算上限，10-15 分钟。背景：Resy 事件里那个 Instinct agent 一小时打了 200 次 API，不是恶意，就是没人告诉它该停，结果账号被封。
actions.text_en: Pick one agent you actually run with real API access, even just a key in a script, and add an hourly call cap or a monthly budget to it, 10-15 minutes. Background: in the Resy incident, an Instinct agent made 200 API calls in an hour not out of malice, just because nobody told it to stop, and the account got banned.
actions.source: AI Engineer 大会：Keycard、摩根大通、Dick Hardt 圆桌
actions.source_en: AI Engineer NYC: Keycard, JPMorgan Chase and Dick Hardt panel

actions.text: 把你现在共用的那一把 AI API key，按用途拆成至少两把（比如“写代码”和“日常聊天”分开），这样月底才知道钱花在哪，15 分钟。背景：Featherless AI 说三到四成找他们的客户，一开始就是一把 key 全公司共用，根本不知道钱花哪了。
actions.text_en: Split whichever AI API key you currently share across different uses into at least two (say, one for coding and one for everyday chat), so you can actually tell where the money went at month's end, 15 minutes. Background: Featherless AI says 30-40% of the customers who come to them started with one shared key for the whole organization and had no idea where the spend was going.
actions.source: AI Engineer 大会：Eugene Cheah（Featherless AI）Token 经济学 workshop
actions.source_en: AI Engineer NYC: Eugene Cheah (Featherless AI) tokenomics workshop

hands_on.title: 上 llmspeed.dev 查你的硬件能跑多快的开源模型
hands_on.title_en: Check llmspeed.dev for how fast your hardware runs today's open models
hands_on.why: 今晚的 token 经济学 workshop 里有一个点很实在：同样的智能，开源模型现在便宜十倍不止，但“我的笔记本/显卡到底能跑多快”这件事，大多数人只能猜。这个开源小站把硬件和模型配对，给出实测或推算的生成速度，先看数字，再决定要不要换模型或买新硬件。
hands_on.why_en: Tonight's tokenomics workshop made one point stick: the same intelligence now costs ten times less or more in open models, but most people are still just guessing at how fast their own laptop or GPU would actually run one. This small open-source site pairs hardware with models and gives a measured or projected generation speed, so you see a number before deciding to switch models or buy new hardware.
steps: 在“Browse by hardware”里找自己现在用的设备（比如 MacBook Pro M5 Max、RTX 4090，没有完全 match 的选最接近的那一款）
在“Browse by model”里选一个你关心的模型，比如今天刚更新的 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash，或者 GLM-5.3 Flash
看页面给出的 tokens/秒估算，页面底部会标明这个数字来自社区实测（r/LocalLLaMA、localscore.ai）还是同类硬件推算
好奇怎么实现的，可以翻开源代码：https://github.com/nicorobinreal/llmspeed
steps_en: Under "Browse by hardware," find the device you actually use (e.g. MacBook Pro M5 Max, RTX 4090; pick the closest match if yours isn't listed exactly)
Under "Browse by model," pick one you care about, e.g. today's updated DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, or GLM-5.3 Flash
Read the tokens/sec estimate the page gives; the footer states whether that number comes from a community benchmark (r/LocalLLaMA, localscore.ai) or a projection from similar hardware
Curious how it's built? The source is open: https://github.com/nicorobinreal/llmspeed

meta_read:
今晚几条新闻放在一起看，说的是同一件事的两头。一头是“该让 agent 干什么”，正从口头信任变成写进协议和日志的硬约束：Keycard、摩根大通和 Dick Hardt 在台上讨论的意图化授权、AAuth 的预算机制，想解决的都是 Resy 事件里那种“没人告诉它该停”的问题。另一头是 OpenCode 这次泄露提醒：你信任的那个“帮你存 key”的云端服务，本身也是要被约束的对象，不是信了 logo 就能放心。同一天，Vercel 的网关数据说，企业早就不在乎谁是前沿了：九月将近三分之一的团队换了自己最常用的实验室，开源模型吃掉七成 token 却只花两成三的钱。模型正在变成随时能换的零件，忠诚度在消失。Cohere 这时候拿下 Aisle（准确说是签了意向书），等于在模型能力之外，再卖一份“谁来保证这套系统是安全的”的答案。

另一条线是怎么把“花了多少钱”这件事说清楚。Eugene Cheah workshop 开场第一句就是：不 measure，后面全是瞎猜。他举的例子（5 个人烧到 15 万美元一个月，换个模型降到 1 万以内）是他自己客户的个案，不是审计结果，他本身也卖推理算力，立场写在明面上。但“先按用途拆开 key 记账”这一步跟立场无关，谁都能今晚就做，详见今日行动。
meta_read_en:
Tonight's stories, put side by side, are really about the same thing from two ends. One end is what an agent is allowed to do, which is moving from spoken trust into hard constraints written into protocols and logs: the intent-based authorization Keycard, JPMorgan Chase and Dick Hardt discuss on stage, and AAuth's budget mechanism, are both trying to fix the exact problem from the Resy incident, nobody told the agent to stop. The other end is what tonight's OpenCode breach is a reminder of: the cloud service you trust to hold your keys for you is itself something that needs constraining, not something you can trust just because of its logo. The same day, Vercel's gateway data says enterprises have stopped caring who's frontier: almost one in three teams changed their most-used lab in September, and open-weight models now take 71.5% of tokens for 23% of spend. The model is becoming a swappable part, and loyalty is disappearing. Cohere picking up Aisle right now (more precisely, signing a letter of intent) amounts to selling a second answer, on top of model capability, of who guarantees this system is secure.

The second thread is how to actually account for what you're spending. Eugene Cheah's workshop opens with one line: without measuring, everything after is a guess. His example (a 5-person team burning $150k a month, down to under $10k after switching models) is his own client's case, not an audited result, and he sells inference himself, which he discloses upfront. But splitting your key by use case and tracking it doesn't depend on that bias, and anyone can do it tonight (see today's actions).

items.title: AI Engineer 大会：给 agent“按次授权”，不是给一把钥匙
items.title_en: AI Engineer NYC: authorize agents per call, not with one master key
items.author: AI Engineer 大会 · Ian Livingstone（Keycard CEO）、Michael Davis（摩根大通全球首席安全架构师）、Dick Hardt（AAuth 创始人，OAuth 2.0 编辑者）
items.author_en: AI Engineer NYC · Ian Livingstone (Keycard CEO), Michael Davis (JPMorgan Chase Global Chief Security Architect), Dick Hardt (AAuth founder, OAuth 2.0 editor)
items.summary: 我读完了整段文字稿（约 9300 词）。这是 AI Engineer 纽约大会上的一场圆桌，主题是给 agent 按次授权，三位嘉宾分别来自身份创业公司、大银行和老牌授权协议。核心问题：OAuth 当年为网页设计，scope 很粗（比如 Notion 的 MCP server，只能整页抓，不能只拿页面里的一个数据库），而 agent 需要的是这一次具体干什么这种细粒度授权，环境又会随时变。三方给出的做法叫意图化授权（intent-based authorization）：每个 agent 的任务先定一个 mission（任务标识），所有后续决策都挂在这个 mission 下面，方便事后审计；授权判断发生在 brains（模型本身）和 hands（真正能执行、带凭证的沙箱）之间的 egress proxy 上，模型本身永远拿不到长期有效的 API key。具体案例：一个 Instinct agent 代用户去 Resy 订餐，一小时打了 200 次 API 调用，不是恶意，就是没人告诉它该停，账号被封。Dick Hardt（OAuth 2.0 的编辑者，现在做 agent 授权新协议 AAuth）据此提出预算概念：给 agent 一个有时间限制的 token，外加一个消耗预算上限，消耗接近上限时持续给 agent 反馈，而不是像传统限流那样直接一刀切断掉（断了 agent 也不知道为什么）。另外提到篡改不了的审计日志要放在 agent 管不到的地方，理由是责任最终要落到雇用这个 agent 的人或机构身上，不是 agent 自己。结尾被问到 AI 末日概率（p(doom)），四人态度都偏向可控，更担心的是内部人恶意滥用，而不是 agent 自己选择作恶。
items.summary_en: I read the full transcript (about 9,300 words). This is an AI Engineer NYC panel on per-call authorization for agents, with an identity startup, a major bank, and an elder OAuth figure on stage. Core problem: OAuth was built for the web and its scopes are coarse (their example: Notion's MCP server can only fetch a whole page, not pull one database inside it), but agents need fine-grained, task-specific authorization in an environment that keeps changing. Their fix is called intent-based authorization: each agent task gets a tracked "mission" ID that every later decision attaches to for audit purposes; authorization decisions happen at an egress proxy between the "brains" (the model itself) and "hands" (the sandboxed, credentialed execution), so the model itself never holds a long-lived API key. Concrete case: an Instinct agent booking a restaurant on behalf of a user made 200 API calls to Resy in an hour, not maliciously, just because nobody told it to stop, and the account got banned. Dick Hardt (who edited OAuth 2.0 and now builds a new agent-authorization protocol called AAuth) responds to this with a "budget" concept: give the agent a time-limited token plus a consumption cap, and give it continuous feedback as it nears the cap, instead of traditional rate-limiting that just cuts it off with no explanation. They also flag that a tamper-resistant audit log needs to sit outside what the agent itself can touch, because liability ultimately falls on whoever employs the agent, not on the agent. Asked about p(doom) at the end, all four panelists leaned toward "this is manageable," more worried about malicious insiders than about an agent itself "choosing" to do harm.
items.why: Keycard 本身就卖这套意图化授权，上台讲这个有自卖自夸的成分。但 Resy 这起事件是能独立核实的真实事故，egress proxy、brains/hands 分离这套架构，Anthropic 和 OpenAI 也在各自做，不是 Keycard 一家编出来的说法。能直接抄的是预算机制：给任何自己在跑的 agent 加一个消耗上限，而不是等它自己闯祸，详见今日行动第 2 条。
items.why_en: Keycard sells exactly this intent-based authorization product, so there's self-promotion baked into the pitch. But the Resy incident is independently verifiable, and the egress-proxy, brains/hands-separation architecture isn't something Keycard invented alone, Anthropic and OpenAI are independently building versions of the same pattern. What transfers directly is the budget mechanism: put a consumption cap on any agent you actually run, instead of waiting for it to cause damage (see action 2).

items.title: AI Engineer 大会：Token 经济学 workshop，先 measure 再谈省钱
items.title_en: AI Engineer NYC: a tokenomics workshop — measure before you optimize
items.author: AI Engineer 大会 · Eugene Cheah（Featherless AI 创始人兼 CEO）
items.author_en: AI Engineer NYC · Eugene Cheah (Featherless AI founder & CEO)
items.summary: 我读完了整段文字稿（约 9800 词）。Eugene Cheah 是 Featherless AI（卖推理算力）的创始人，一开场就说清楚自己的立场：讲的东西会偏向卖推理这件事。他给了一套四步法：先 measure（先按部门/用途拆开 API key，很多来找他们的客户一开始就是全公司一把 key 共用，根本不知道钱花哪了），再 right-size（按 workload 类型区分：agentic coding 这种长上下文、高缓存命中率的任务，和 call center、文档审核这种高并发、短上下文的 process 型任务，经济模型完全不同），再决定怎么买算力（同样的硬件，要速度就要多花钱，他给的经验是速度翻倍，成本翻三倍，所以后台跑的 agent 不该配跟人聊天一样的速度），最后检查流程本身有没有在制造浪费。具体数字：一个 5 人团队连续跑 8 个 agent，原来全用 Opus 4.8 的 API，一个月烧 15 万美元，换成开源模型（转写成 GRM 5.3，结合今晚其他来源的拼写应为 GLM-5.3）单节点就降到 1 万美元以内，没感觉到变慢；一家电信客户把推理成本从每月 25 万降到 7600 美元；一个 2 万亿 token/天的客户，用 512 块 AMD MI215 跑私有模型，价格压到每百万 token 0.03 美元，接近 Opus 4.8 水准。他还提了个概念叫甩锅弹（slop grenade）：生成一堆东西甩给别人收拾，他的规矩是谁生成谁负责，这条东西出了问题是生成的人的责任，不是 agent 的。关于产出：他提到一些组织反映 AI 实际生产力提升只有 6% 到 7%，跟预想的差很远，原因是有了锤子看什么都像钉子，到处乱用。
items.summary_en: I read the full transcript (about 9,800 words). Eugene Cheah, founder of Featherless AI (which sells inference), opens by disclosing his bias: he sells the thing he's about to recommend. His framework has four steps: measure first (split your API key by department/use case; 30-40% of his customers arrive with one shared key for the whole org and no idea where spend goes), then right-size (agentic coding workloads are long-context and cache-heavy; process workloads like call centers or document review are high-concurrency and short-context; the economics differ completely), then decide how to buy capacity (on the same hardware, doubling speed roughly triples cost, so a background agent shouldn't be provisioned at chat-speed), then check whether the process itself is wasting output. Concrete figures: a 5-person team running 8 continuous agents on Opus 4.8's API burned $150k a month; switching to an open model (transcribed as "GRM 5.3," almost certainly GLM-5.3 given tonight's other sources) on a single node brought that under $10k with no felt slowdown. A telecom customer cut inference cost from $250k to $7,600 a month. A customer processing 2 trillion tokens a day on 512 AMD MI215 GPUs running a private model got pricing down to $0.03 per million tokens at roughly Opus-4.8-class performance. He also names a "slop grenade": generating a pile of output and dumping it on someone else to clean up; his rule is whoever generates something owns it, not the agent. On output: he cites organizations reporting only 6-7% real productivity gain, far below expectations, because "everyone just takes the shiny new hammer and hits everything with it."
items.why: Eugene Cheah 卖的就是推理算力，换开源模型省钱这个结论，立场摆在明面上，15 万到 1 万、25 万到 7600 这些数字是他客户的个案，不是审计结果。但先拆开 key 按用途记账这一步跟立场无关，谁都能今晚就做，详见今日行动第 3 条。
items.why_en: Eugene Cheah sells inference, and "switch to open models to save money" is a conclusion that serves his business, which he discloses upfront; the $150k-to-$10k and $250k-to-$7,600 figures are his own client anecdotes, not audited results. But "split your key by use case and track it" doesn't depend on that bias, and anyone can do it tonight (see action 3).

items.title: OpenCode 云端服务密钥泄露，官方说影响 1.4% 用户
items.title_en: OpenCode's hosted service leaks keys, company says 1.4% of users affected
items.author: OpenCode（官方声明）· Hacker News
items.summary: OpenCode（Anomaly 开发的开源 coding agent）在 X 上发声明称：昨晚发现一套正在下线的老系统遭人未授权访问，用户存在 OpenCode Console（其托管的、类似 OpenRouter 的代理服务）里的第三方 key（OpenAI、Anthropic 等）可能已泄露，已给受影响用户发邮件。官方称影响 1.4% 的用户，正联系 Anthropic、OpenAI、Google 一起处理，细节暂不公开。HN 评论区做了两件事：一是指出此事只影响用 OpenCode Console 托管服务的人，本地跑 CLI、自己存 key 的人不受影响（但有条未经证实的评论说，就算本地用，agent 也可能把 .env 文件读进去，存疑）；二是质疑官方所称的大规模蒸馏攻击，认为公司没给出任何证据支撑这个具体说法，只是一句话定性。还有人翻出 68 天前自己在 HN 提醒过 OpenCode 的数据处理方式有问题，现在看是提前预警。
items.summary_en: OpenCode (the open-source coding agent built by Anomaly) posted its own statement on X: it found unauthorized access overnight to a legacy system it was in the process of decommissioning, and third-party keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) stored in OpenCode Console, its hosted OpenRouter-like proxy service, may have been exposed. It emailed affected users, says 1.4% of users were hit, and is working with Anthropic, OpenAI and Google, with no further details public yet. The HN comment thread did two things: first, it pinned down that this only affects people using the hosted Console service, not those running the CLI locally with their own keys (though one unverified comment claims local .env files could also have been read by agents, flagged as unconfirmed); second, it pushed back on the official framing of a "large-scale distillation attack," noting the company offered no evidence for that specific claim, just an assertion. One commenter also surfaced their own HN warning from 68 days earlier about OpenCode's data practices, which now reads as an early flag.
items.why: 能核实的只有公司自己的声明，和 HN 事后把 Console 云端服务与本地 CLI 这两件事分清楚的技术纠偏，没有第三方安全公司的独立报告。大规模蒸馏攻击这个说法，公司自己也没给证据。能直接抄的教训是：任何帮你托管 API key 的云服务，都要当成会泄露来对待，详见今日行动第 1 条。
items.why_en: What's verifiable here is only the company's own statement, plus HN's after-the-fact technical correction separating the hosted Console service from the local CLI. There's no independent security-firm report, and the company gave no evidence for its own "large-scale distillation attack" framing. What transfers directly: treat any cloud service that holds your API keys for you as something that will eventually leak (see action 1).

items.title: 苹果官方实测：4 台 Mac Studio 跑 8160 亿参数模型，每秒 36 个 token
items.title_en: Apple's own benchmark: an 816B-parameter model at 36 tokens/sec across 4 Mac Studios
items.author: Apple Machine Learning Research
items.summary: 苹果 ML Research 团队发文，用当天刚发布的 MLX 新版本，实测跑 Meta 同一天放出的开源模型 Muse Spark Open（总参数 8160 亿，激活 420 亿的 MoE 模型，NVFP4 量化）。单台 Mac Studio（最高 512GB 统一内存）就能跑起来，4 台 M5 Ultra 的 Mac Studio 用新出的 Thunderbolt RDMA 驱动组成集群，上下文 8192 token 时，生成速度超过每秒 36 个 token，高于普通人阅读速度。文章同时测了 Mistral Medium 3.5（1280 亿参数，稠密模型）和 Qwen 3.8（270 亿参数，稠密模型），对比 M5 Ultra 和上一代 M3 Ultra 在首字延迟、吞吐量、峰值功耗上的差别。独立测评方 Artificial Analysis 给 Muse Spark Open 打了 39 分（Intelligence Index），在美国开源模型里排第一，但落后于中国的 GLM-5.3（45 分）和 Kimi K3（44 分）；上线定价是 Together、Fireworks、Baseten 上每百万输入/输出 token 1.25 美元/4.25 美元。
items.summary_en: Apple's ML Research team published a post benchmarking Meta's newly released open-weight model, Muse Spark Open (816B total parameters, 42B active, a NVFP4-quantized MoE), using a new version of MLX released the same day. A single Mac Studio (up to 512GB unified memory) can run it; a cluster of four M5 Ultra Mac Studios, using a new RDMA-over-Thunderbolt driver, generates over 36 tokens/sec at an 8,192-token context, above average human reading speed. The post also benchmarks Mistral Medium 3.5 (128B, dense) and Qwen 3.8 (27B, dense), comparing M5 Ultra against the previous-generation M3 Ultra on time-to-first-token, throughput, and peak power. Independent evaluator Artificial Analysis scores Muse Spark Open 39 on its Intelligence Index, ranking it first among US open-weight models but behind China's GLM-5.3 (45) and Kimi K3 (44); launch pricing on Together, Fireworks and Baseten is $1.25/$4.25 per million input/output tokens.
items.why: 这是苹果自己发的测试，但量化方式、上下文长度、硬件台数都写清楚了，比很多能在本地跑的宣传更诚实。第一的分数也标明是 Artificial Analysis 给的第三方分数，不是苹果自己打的，而且写出了落后 GLM-5.3 和 Kimi K3 这件事，不是只讲好的一面。想知道自己的设备能跑多快，别只看这篇，去今日上手里的 llmspeed.dev 查一下。
items.why_en: This is Apple's own test, but it states quantization, context length and hardware count clearly, more honest than a lot of "runs locally" marketing. The #1 ranking is explicitly Artificial Analysis's third-party score, not Apple's own, and the post states it trails GLM-5.3 and Kimi K3 rather than only showing the flattering side. To find out how fast your own hardware would actually run it, don't stop at this post, check llmspeed.dev under tonight's hands-on.

items.title: Vercel 网关数据：开源模型吃掉七成 token，只花两成三的钱
items.title_en: Vercel's gateway data: open-weight models take 71.5% of tokens for 23% of spend
items.author: Amelia Charles、Harpreet Arora（Vercel）· TLDR AI
items.author_en: Amelia Charles, Harpreet Arora (Vercel) · TLDR AI
items.summary: Vercel 每月发一份基于自家 AI Gateway 真实流量的报告。这期（10 月刊，覆盖 9 月数据）的几个数字：开源模型现在处理网关七成以上（71.5%）的 token，花掉接近四分之一（23%）的钱，这个花钱占比从 6 月到 9 月翻了四倍多。DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 一家就吃掉 9 月近一半的 token，却只花了 2.6% 的钱，单价大约是开源模型平均价的五分之一。9 月将近三分之一的付费团队换了自己最常用的那家实验室（lab），创了这份报告的纪录。TypeSafe AI 的 Jev（一个决策模型）是网关史上采用最快的模型，上线头两周进了 35% 付费团队的工作流，但只占了 1% 的 token 和 0.15% 的花费；反过来，Opus 5.5 上线头两周就拿走 11% 的网关美元，是 9 月所有新模型里拿钱最多的一个。Anthropic 整体的花费占比从 8 月的 63.7% 掉到 9 月的 43.9%，头一次跌破五成。另外，9 月近七成花在中国模型（Moonshot、DeepSeek、Z.ai）上的钱，走的是美国本土的供应商，12 月这个比例还不到一成。
items.summary_en: Vercel publishes a monthly report based on real traffic through its own AI Gateway. This issue (October, covering September data): open-weight models now process more than 71.5% of gateway tokens and take nearly a quarter (23%) of spend, a share that has more than quadrupled since June. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash alone processed nearly half of September's tokens while taking just 2.6% of spend, at roughly a fifth of the open-weight average price. Almost one in three paid teams changed their most-used lab in September, a record for the index. TypeSafe AI's Jev, a "decision model," is the fastest-adopted model in the gateway's history, reaching 35% of paid teams in its first two weeks, but it accounted for only 1% of tokens and 0.15% of spend; conversely, Opus 5.5 took 11% of gateway dollars in its own first two weeks, the largest spend share of any September launch. Anthropic's overall spend share fell from 63.7% in August to 43.9% in September, the first time it dropped below half. Separately, nearly 70% of September's spend on Chinese-origin models (Moonshot, DeepSeek, Z.ai) was routed through US-based providers, up from under 10% in December.
items.why: 这些数字是 Vercel 自己网关上的真实流量，不是调查问卷，但只覆盖走它家网关的那部分市场，不是全行业。价格按官方标价估算，不是实际账单。能看出的方向很清楚：企业不再为谁是前沿付溢价，模型正变成随时能换的零件，忠诚度在消失。
items.why_en: These numbers come from real traffic on Vercel's own gateway, not a survey, but they only cover the slice of the market that runs through that gateway, not the whole industry; pricing is estimated at list price, not actual bills. The direction is clear regardless: enterprises are no longer paying a premium for "being frontier," the model is becoming a swappable part, and loyalty is disappearing.

items.title: Cohere 签意向书收购 Aisle，防御性安全 agent 一年找了 500 多个 CVE
items.title_en: Cohere signs letter of intent to acquire Aisle, whose defensive agent found 500+ CVEs in a year
items.author: Cohere Team · TLDR AI
items.summary: Cohere 博客原文用的是 proposed agreement、proposed transaction，即已签意向书、尚未完成交割，并非 HN 标题和 Aidan Gomez 推文所暗示的已完成收购。Aisle 2024 年成立于布拉格，做的是用 AI 自动发现、验证并协助修复生产软件中未知漏洞的系统。结束 stealth 第一年，Aisle 找到 500 多个经 CVE 确认的未知漏洞，覆盖 100 多个代码库，包括 OpenSSL 今年 1 月安全发布中的全部 12 个漏洞，以及 curl 最新一次发布 24 个 CVE 中的 18 个；这些漏洞均经对应软件维护者独立复核确认，并非自说自话。交易完成后，Aisle 三位创始人进入 Cohere 管理层：Ondrej Vlcek 任新成立的 Cohere Cyber 负责人，Jaya Baloo 任 Cohere 首席信息安全官，Stanislav Fort 任 AI 安全副总裁；Cohere 计划在布拉格长期加码投资。Cohere 称这是继收购 Reliant AI 和 Aleph Alpha 之后，在欧洲主权 AI 方向的第三次收购。
items.summary_en: Cohere's own blog post uses the words "proposed agreement" and "proposed transaction," meaning a signed letter of intent, not a completed deal the way HN's headline and Aidan Gomez's tweet made it sound. Aisle, founded in 2024 and based in Prague, builds AI systems that discover, validate and help remediate previously unknown vulnerabilities in production software. In its first year out of stealth, Aisle found more than 500 previously unknown vulnerabilities assigned CVEs across 100+ codebases, including all 12 vulnerabilities in OpenSSL's January security release and 18 of the 24 CVEs in curl's latest release, each independently reviewed and confirmed by the relevant software maintainers, not self-reported. If the deal closes, Aisle's three founders take leadership roles at Cohere: Ondrej Vlcek heads the newly formed Cohere Cyber business, Jaya Baloo becomes Cohere's CISO, and Stanislav Fort becomes VP of AI Security; Cohere plans a long-term investment expansion in Prague. Cohere states this is its third acquisition aimed at European sovereign AI, after Reliant AI and Aleph Alpha.
items.why: HN 标题和公司 CEO 自己的推文都写的是收购完成，读 Cohere 博客原文才看出是提议中的交易，尚未签完。Aisle 找到的 CVE 数字经软件维护者独立确认，属硬数据，不是公司自吹。能看出的趋势是：安全能力正成为 AI 公司给自己加的一道独立护城河，不只是模型跑分。
items.why_en: The HN headline and the CEO's own tweet both read as a completed acquisition; only reading Cohere's own blog post shows it's actually a "proposed transaction," not yet signed and closed. The CVE count Aisle reports is independently confirmed by software maintainers, so that part is hard data, not a company bragging about itself. The visible trend: security capability is becoming its own moat for AI companies, separate from model benchmark scores.

learned: 今晚 HN 排名第一的是 Claude 破解 NSA 加密曲线种子来源那篇（anthropic.com），48 小时内涨到 1023 分，为整晚最高。但翻昨天（10-16）那期自己记的落选清单才发现，同一 URL 昨天已经看过、读过，并明确写为偏研究趣闻，不在应用/GTM 这条选题倾向里；今天既无新事实也无新角度，只是分数从 648 涨到 1023。分数涨是因为更多人点了 upvote，新闻本身没有变新。
已把这条规则写进 daily-digest/SKILL.md：选高分候选前，先查最近一两期自己的 ota.learned 落选清单，不只查 ota-ledger.md。两者查的是不同的事：ledger 记的是这条消息是假的；这次要查的是这条消息是真的，但不符合选题倾向，已经判过一次。

AI Engineer 大会那场授权圆桌的自动字幕，把 Dick Hardt 打成了 Dick Hart，把他的 AAuth 协议打成了 AOTH，把 OAuth 打成了 OOTH。查证后确认：Dick Hardt 是 OAuth 2.0（RFC 6749）的编辑者，现在提的 AAuth 是他为 agent 做的新授权草案。Keycard 那位只被喊了 Ian，查到全名是 Ian Livingstone。语音转写人名，没查证就直接按听到的打，是会出错的。
HN 和 TLDR 都把 Cohere 拿下 Aisle 写成已完成收购，翻 Cohere 博客原文才发现，用的词是 proposed agreement、proposed transaction，即已签意向书、尚未完成交割。标题常比原文走得更快一步。
learned_en: Tonight's #1-scoring HN story was the one about Claude tracing the NSA's elliptic-curve seed origins (anthropic.com), which climbed to 1023 points within 48 hours, the highest score of the night. But reading yesterday's (10-16) own cut-list first showed this exact URL had already been swept, read, and explicitly written off as 'a research curiosity, off this digest's applied/GTM tilt.' Nothing new tonight, no new facts, no new angle, just more upvotes (648 -> 1023). A rising score means more people clicked upvote, not that the news got fresher.

Added this rule to daily-digest/SKILL.md: before picking an unusually high-scoring candidate, check the last one or two issues' own ota.learned cut-list, not just ota-ledger.md. The two check different things: the ledger records 'this story is false'; this check is for 'this story is true but was already judged off-tilt once.'

The AI Engineer NYC panel's auto-captions transcribed Dick Hardt as 'Dick Hart,' his AAuth protocol as 'AOTH,' and OAuth as 'OOTH.' Checking confirmed: Dick Hardt edited OAuth 2.0 (RFC 6749), and AAuth is his new draft authorization protocol for agents. Keycard's panelist was only heard as 'Ian'; a search confirmed Ian Livingstone. Transcribing a spoken name as heard, without checking it, is a real way to get it wrong.

Both HN and TLDR wrote 'Cohere acquires Aisle' as a done deal. Reading Cohere's own blog post showed the actual language is 'proposed agreement' and 'proposed transaction' — a signed letter of intent, not a closed acquisition. A secondary headline often runs ahead of what the primary source actually says.
new_capabilities: 已实施：daily-digest/SKILL.md 去重部分新增一条：选任何分数异常高的候选前，先 grep 最近一两期 digest JSON 里的 ota.learned/learned_en 数组，查有没有被同一选题倾向明确判过 off-tilt。这是对已有 grep ota-ledger.md 查假消息规则的补充，查的是另一种情况：消息是真的，但已经被判过不符合选题倾向。
new_capabilities_en: Implemented: added a line to daily-digest/SKILL.md's dedup section — before adding any unusually high-scoring candidate, grep the last 1-2 digest JSONs' ota.learned/learned_en arrays for an explicit same-tilt 'off-tilt' rejection. This complements the existing 'grep ota-ledger.md for a debunk' rule by covering a different case: the story is true, but has already been judged off this digest's tilt once.
